title: StorageEngine 書き込み (CreatePool/Volume/Snapshot, special vdev バリデーション)

planning.decision: Kept the three pre-planned stories (Pool create + validation, Volume/Preset/Snapshot, Import). Each maps to a coherent user-visible behavior; splitting further would have produced sub-stories smaller than the test scaffolding they needed.
planning.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority #5 (信頼性 > 機能) — keep validation rule changes in the same Story as the create flow they protect.

planning.decision: Excluded DestroyPool / DestroyVolume / wipe operations. Only create / import / snapshot / rollback in scope.
planning.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority #5 + sprint brief: destructive ops require a name-typing confirmation UX which is not yet built. Adding the engine method without the dialog would invite accidental wiring.

implementation.decision: ValidatePoolConfig returns ErrSpecialNotRedundant unless cfg.ForceNoRedundancy is set. UI never sets it (the form has no field). CLI exposes --force-no-redundancy on `kura storage create-pool` only.
implementation.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES forbidden #3 (single SSD special = error, not warning) + forbidden #14 (force flow only via CLI flag). Test: TestValidatePoolConfig/err_special_vdev_single_SSD.

implementation.decision: Sourced from docs/initial-input/Kuraos-design.md §4.4. Used compression=zstd for all three presets (CLAUDE.md hint mentioned lz4 for media/database; design.md §4.4 says zstd; design.md is the authoritative document).
implementation.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority #2 (賢いデフォルト > 設定項目を増やす) — preset is opaque to user. Keeping a single compressor (zstd) reduces variance; modern hardware absorbs CPU cost.

implementation.decision: PresetDatabase sets LogBias="latency" in addition to recordsize=16K, special_small_blocks=64K. Other presets leave LogBias empty (ZFS default).
implementation.rationale: design.md §4.4 explicitly notes (logbias=latency) for database. Saves the operator from a foot-gun where DB workloads stall on indirect-sync writes.

implementation.decision: ImportPool issues `zpool import -d /dev/disk/by-id -N <name>` first (dry-run, no mount), then `zpool import -d /dev/disk/by-id <name>` if dry-run succeeds. Same flag set is reused for both calls.
implementation.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority #5: surface ZFS feature-flag mismatch / availability problems before mounting datasets. Two-step flow gives a clean rollback boundary.

implementation.decision: ImportOpts.Force is wired only when the form sends `force=1`. The import modal renders an unchecked checkbox with warning copy. UI never produces a one-click force.
implementation.rationale: Forbidden #14: force flow not reachable as one-click UX. Acceptance test TestAcceptance_StorageImportPool asserts default Force=false; TestAcceptance_StorageImportPool_ForceFlow asserts the explicit opt-in path.

implementation.decision: Kept Engine interface monolithic (read + write) but added separate ui.StorageEngineReader / StorageEngineWriter so handlers can opt into write surface. Read tests still inject a stub that does not implement Writer.
implementation.rationale: DESIGN_PRINCIPLES priority #9 (testability) — small interfaces at the consumer side, single struct implementation on the engine side.

implementation.decision: Validation runs before any CLI shell-out (TestCreatePool_validatesBeforeShell asserts zero calls when validation rejects). Mid-stream zfs failures bubble up wrapped errors; we do not attempt automatic cleanup.
implementation.rationale: Sprint brief: 'Pool/Volume create 失敗時は冪等再試行可能に'. The chosen approach: validate-first prevents partial state; if zpool create itself partially fails ZFS already won't return the pool to the listing, so retry is safe.

implementation.decision: engine/storage/apply.go registers a config.ApplyAdapter for section="storage". Plan emits create_pool / import_pool / create_volume / set_quota steps; pool/volume removal never produces a step.
implementation.rationale: Priority #1 SSOT — pool/volume created via UI must round-trip through config.json export. Destructive omission matches the sprint scope-out.

implementation.decision: Added `kura storage create-pool` with flags: --name, --vdev <layout:disks>, --special, --spares, --small-block, --force-no-redundancy. Subcommand syntax: `mirror:/dev/sda,/dev/sdb`.
implementation.rationale: Sprint brief: 'kura storage create-pool ... [--force-no-redundancy] (この --force-no-redundancy は special vdev single disk を許可する唯一の経路)'. The CLI surface lets a knowledgeable operator perform the override under their own responsibility.

implementation.decision: Surface the dry-run zpool error to the operator wrapped via fmt.Errorf with i18n.MsgStorageErrImportFailed. No auto-upgrade attempt.
implementation.rationale: Priority #5 信頼性: feature upgrades during import are not reversible. Operator must opt in by retrying with appropriate flags from the CLI.

review.decision: All write paths covered by table-driven Go tests with cmdexec.Fake. No real ZFS required. E2E vs VM: deferred to milestone Sd64f38 demo (real ZFS verification).
review.rationale: CLAUDE.md test_environment: dev box has no ZFS, mock everything via cmdexec.Fake; real validation at milestone.

review.decision: None added. The Volume tab UI rendering in the live Storage page is light (button skeletons only) — when tank dataset listing is wired (next sprint), the Volume/Snapshot tabs can render real data.
review.rationale: Volume listing is not in this sprint's scope; the engine surface to list datasets is design.md §4.2 (CreateVolume/SetQuota) but a full ListVolumes is incremental.

warnings.detail: Engine code paths are not exercised against an actual zpool. Any subtle CLI-flag drift between OpenZFS versions would only show at milestone Sd64f38 VM demo.

Storage page renders the New Pool / Import flows and the existing read-only PoolCard / disks table. Volume / Snapshot tabs from the prototype are intentionally minimal — full data wiring waits for the next sprint that adds engine.ListVolumes / engine.ListAllSnapshots.

warnings.topic: Force-no-redundancy CLI flag is a sharp edge
warnings.detail: The --force-no-redundancy escape hatch is documented only in code comments and decisions.json. Operators who do not read the source will not discover it; that's intentional but could trip a power user.

artifacts.test_status: pass (engine/storage 4 test files, all passing; tests/acceptance 6 new sub-tests, all passing; full ./... go test 0 failures)
